course_name_original: SISTEMI ELETTRICI PER LA DISTRIBUZIONE E LA GESTIONE DELL'ENERGIA
course_name_en: ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS FOR ENERGY DISTRIBUTION AND MANAGEMENT

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the fundamental concepts of modern electrical distribution networks, including the presence of renewable energy sources and high penetration of information and communication technologies (Smart Grids).

Acquire knowledge about electrical devices used in the distribution and management of electrical energy, with particular reference to low and medium voltage systems, and technologies for managing distributed energy sources and demand-side energy, even in complex scenarios.
Be able to practically analyze electrical circuits related to the distribution and management of electrical energy.
Be able to use electrotechnical tools to understand the operation of electrical networks for energy distribution and management.
Be able to design low and medium voltage electrical systems in standard application scenarios.
Be able to analyze issues related to the evolution of electrical energy distribution networks towards Smart Grid scenarios.
Be able to identify techniques and methodologies for meeting quality and reliability constraints in distribution networks with distributed sources and electric vehicles.
Be able to use devices and techniques for evaluating electrical quantities in Smart Grids.
Ability to use appropriate mathematical tools for practical purposes.
Ability to analyze electrical distribution systems in various application scenarios.
Ability to analyze problems inherent in distribution networks with distributed sources and choose the most adequate solutions to respect quality and reliability constraints.
Improved self-assessment and ability to manage the solution of a concrete problem with time limits through the execution of unguided sizing and design exercises within a set time.

syllabus_topics: Structure of the electrical system: generation, transmission, distribution, EHV/HV, MV, LV networks

Medium voltage electrical systems: overhead and cable power lines, power transformer in electrical energy systems, faults in three-phase networks, protection in electrical distribution systems, MV/LV electrical substations, electrical safety
Low voltage electrical systems: sizing of electrical conductors and overcurrent and overvoltage protection devices, disconnection and control devices, earthing system, electrical safety
Examples of electrical system design using dedicated software
Critical issues of traditional electrical systems and introduction to Smart Grids
Production and distribution of electricity from renewable sources. Power quality and reliability
Energy management methods in the presence of distributed sources
Devices and techniques for evaluating electrical quantities in Smart Grids
IoT for applications in smart grid and home automation
Application examples in Matlab/Simulink environment and on microcontroller board

assessment_methods.method: Presentation and discussion of a final technical report related to a project

assessment_rules: The final exam is evaluated out of 30, with a possible cum laude. The minimum passing grade is 18/30. A minimum grade of eighteen is awarded for sufficient knowledge of techniques and ability to analyze and solve problems. The maximum grade of thirty is awarded for full autonomy in project execution, problem-solving, and demonstration of functional characteristics through experimental tests. Cum laude is reserved for students showing scientific rigor and brilliant exposition.
